title: Community Dental Services are submitting wait list data, but where is the result?
html:
Over a year since NHS England began collecting wait list data from Community Dental Services (CDS), publication of the results has been delayed as it ‘continues to work through data quality issues’.

NHS England first began collecting data on a national level in August 2025 in order to measure the extent of the access crisis facing Community Dental Services. According to the Health Service Journal, publication of the outcome of this data collection, which had originally been slated to begin from October 2025, has now been delayed to early 2027.

The British Dental Association (BDA) has previously estimated that both children and vulnerable adult patients could be facing year-long waits for treatment through CDS. The association hoped the reporting would provide clarity around the scale of this access crisis and provide evidence for the need for further evidence.

Giten Dabhi, chair of the England Community Dental Service Committee, said: ‘I know from the frontline that waiting times in the CDS are unacceptable, and this new data will turn that anecdote into fact.

‘This is one of the key areas that we outlined in our call to action to make sure community dentistry is finally given the priority it deserves. We asked for greater waiting list transparency on access to CDS services and that the data is published in the same format as other NHS services.’

What is causing the delays?

Several factors could be affecting the quality of the CDS wait list data collected, including consistency of data returned. NHS England said integrated care boards (ICBs), providers and managed clinical networks are reviewing local data, improving return consistency and addressing ‘quality concerns’.

National guidance recommends that providers measure wait times from receipt of referral to the start of first definitive treatment. NHS England has set an action to encourage ICBs to work with providers to ensure these start/stop rules are applied correctly. Different interpretations of the wait time period could affect the comparability of data submitted.

A GRIFT report on CDS services also acknowledged the lack of a consistent CDS data set. It called for better governance and standardisation of performance reporting across services.

Its analysis of initial questionnaire responses found a discrepancy between the number of patients in total wait list data and the number of patients in waiting lists broken down by length of wait. The report said this is a cause for concern as it suggests there are some patients who are waiting for treatment but have not been added to a tracked list.
